GraceChangeDesignContext.NormativeStatus: non-normative; spec.xml wins on every conflict
GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: M1.2 is intentionally retained as one product change because its acceptance claim is indivisible: Worldline does not have a production browser provider until one real packaged CEF process passes the complete S2 path through the ordinary broker and native IPC boundary. Implementation risk is controlled by decomposing the separately approved plan into bounded dependency-ordered packages, not by weakening or multiplying the milestone contract.

ArchitectureSummary.Topology: Worldline host -> generic kernel capability broker and lifecycle -> versioned native plugin protocol -> BrowserEngineProvider with fresh RuntimeId -> provider-private CEF browser-process adapter -> sandboxed renderer/GPU/network/utility/crashpad children.
ArchitectureSummary.Boundary: Public consumers see only engine-neutral serialized Worldline contracts and logical identities.
Generic host extensions know about process containment and blobs, never about browsers or CEF.
The CEF adapter owns FFI, thread affinity, callback translation and native window integration.
Higher-level tabs, history, download, cookie, workspace and UI policy remains in future service plugins.

ProcessContainmentDecision.Decision: Extend the generic native host with a process-containment abstraction established before child code can spawn descendants.
ProcessContainmentDecision.WindowsDirection: Use a Job Object or equivalent kill-on-close ownership mechanism and test nested-job behavior on hosted Windows.
ProcessContainmentDecision.OtherPlatforms: Provide an explicit process-group/containment implementation or report unsupported real-provider status; do not fake equivalent evidence.
ProcessContainmentDecision.Reason: A hard-killed provider cannot reliably reap its own renderer/GPU/network children, and current NativeChild kill owns only the direct process.

CefBootstrapDecision.Decision: The executable runs CEF subprocess dispatch before parsing or opening Worldline provider IPC.
The production browser process uses one documented CEF message-loop strategy and sends thread-affine work through a bounded dispatcher.
No global provider or kernel lifecycle lock is held while waiting for CEF, and callbacks cannot re-enter while a global provider mutex is held.
Shutdown stops admission, resolves or marks pending requests, drains bounded dispatch, shuts down CEF, then closes containment.

RevisionReservationDecision.Decision: DocumentRevision is a durable logical generation, not a count inferred from a CEF browser, frame, navigation or process identifier.
RevisionReservationDecision.Sequence: engine reports a new or restored top-level document -> provider reserves next generation by installation-state CAS -> provider binds engine document to that generation -> provider marks page ready -> provider may return/publish the generation and issue ElementRefs.
RevisionReservationDecision.CrashWindow: If CEF changed the page but the reservation/completion boundary is unknown, the operation is Incomplete and the page remains unready until a further durable generation is reserved.
RevisionReservationDecision.DynamicDom: Within one document generation, detached or replaced engine nodes fail live-node validation even when the enclosing document revision still matches.

BlobArtifactDecision.Decision: Add bounded generic native BlobPut/BlobGet/BlobVerify host requests rather than encoding screenshots in StateRequest or exposing filesystem paths.
BlobArtifactDecision.Authority: Each host request is bound to the current runtime and an attenuated invocation/resource handle; stale or foreign handles fail.
BlobArtifactDecision.PublicIdentity: The browser capture contract returns a provider-owned artifact identity mapped to BlobId in installation state; BlobId knowledge is not read authority.
BlobArtifactDecision.ReadFlow: The caller uses an authorized capture-artifact read operation; the provider performs the scoped host blob read and returns bounded chunks.
BlobArtifactDecision.Reason: This reuses the existing crash-safe content-addressed BlobStore without creating browser storage inside the kernel.

SecurityDefaults.Default: CEF sandbox enabled and no production no-sandbox flag.
No ambient remote-debugging listener; test diagnostics, if needed, are separately gated and loopback-only.
CEF libraries and resources load only from the checksum-pinned package root.
HTTP, HTTPS and about:blank form the minimum navigation surface; file, javascript, chrome, devtools and undeclared custom schemes fail closed.
Provider filesystem use is confined to package assets, installation-owned profiles, ephemeral incognito roots and authorized staging/blob flows.
CEF children inherit no Worldline stdio protocol endpoints, opaque host handles, principal/grant values or reusable environment secrets.
SecurityDefaults.Limitation: The provider is trusted native code; where the generic native host lacks a complete OS sandbox, the project reports that limitation rather than equating capability checks with exploit containment.

PermissionFlow.Sequence: authorized browser.permission set RPC -> validate ContextId and canonical origin -> persist/update provider decision projection -> CEF permission callback performs bounded local lookup -> missing or Prompt-without-policy becomes Denied -> post-outcome event may report the decision.
PermissionFlow.Reason: A CEF callback requires an immediate answer; an event subscriber cannot be promoted into an RPC decision-maker.

EventOwnership.Owner: page creation/closure/readiness, navigation facts, document generation change, action outcome, renderer failure and completed restore.
runtime failure, authority revocation, restart, quarantine, staged switch and generic health transition.
EventOwnership.Projection: A new provider may emit page-restored/ready only after it has reopened installation state and durably rebound pages; it does not claim to have witnessed the old runtime's death.

ProfileAndRecoveryModel.Persistent: Logical profile metadata and page checkpoints live in installation state; Chromium databases remain provider-owned external state beneath a confined installation root.
ProfileAndRecoveryModel.Incognito: Ephemeral roots are never referenced by durable restore state and are scavenged after abnormal termination.
ProfileAndRecoveryModel.Checkpoint: Persist ContextId, PageId ownership, last committed URL, durable next-generation state, bounded engine navigation recovery data and selected-page projection.
ProfileAndRecoveryModel.NotHistory: The checkpoint exists only for crash restore and is not the durable user history service.

HeadfulAndPlatformPolicy.Decision: Windows x86_64 native/windowed/headful is the first real acceptance path because it minimizes composition risk before M1.4.
The proving window is provider-owned and minimal; HWND never enters a browser contract or identity.
OSR/wgpu remains deferred and cannot block the windowed provider.
HeadfulAndPlatformPolicy.ClaimPolicy: Linux may compile and test engine-neutral/provider-state code, but no real Linux CEF claim exists without named evidence.

Package.Name: Architecture and compatibility freeze
Package.Contents: Provider ADR, exact contract delta fixtures, package/version choice, security and platform decisions.
Package.Exit: All later package scopes can be derived without changing the approved spec or plan.

Package.Name: Generic native host prerequisites
Package.Contents: Process-tree containment, bounded blob host calls, runtime-scoped authority and compatibility/security tests.
Package.Exit: No browser naming or CEF type enters generic kernel/protocol/host APIs.

Package.Name: Provider core and reference backend
Package.Contents: Engine-neutral state machines, contract dispatch, budgets, identities, revision reservation, persistence and normal native IPC path.
Package.Exit: Context/page/navigation/observe and events pass out-of-process without CEF.

Package.Name: CEF package, bootstrap and headful rendering
Package.Contents: Pinned package acquisition, FFI adapter, child dispatch, thread model, sandbox/security defaults and deterministic local windowed navigation.
Package.Exit: Real CEF renders the loopback fixture through the ordinary provider process.

Package.Name: Semantic query, action and capture
Package.Contents: Bounded AX/DOM projection, live node bindings, safe actions, capture artifact path and compatibility tests.
Package.Exit: Exact ElementRef action and authorized capture work through IPC with bounded results.

Package.Name: Profiles and engine primitives
Package.Contents: Persistent/incognito contexts, cookie/storage primitives, permissions, download staging and privacy/path negative tests.
Package.Exit: Profile isolation and fail-closed permission/download behavior are proven.

Package.Name: Recovery, health and upgrade
Package.Contents: Renderer/provider/host recovery, orphan cleanup, health/backpressure, staged switch and truthful rollback limits.
Package.Exit: Fresh RuntimeId and revision safety hold across every crash path.

Package.Name: S2 and CI closure
Package.Contents: Repository BrowserProvider suite, hosted Windows job, complete clean-host S2, regression gates and final GRACE/ROADMAP reconciliation.
Package.Exit: Named local and hosted evidence supports M1.2 Done.

Alternatives.Alternative: Split M1.2 into multiple independent GraceChangeSpecs. Rejected because partial bundles could imply a production provider before S2; bounded plan packages provide the required execution isolation under one acceptance contract.
Let the CEF provider own cleanup of its descendants. Rejected because a hard-killed provider cannot guarantee cleanup.
Store screenshots as StateRequest payloads or raw paths. Rejected because state, blobs and filesystem authority have distinct owners and failure semantics.
Replace Browser Contract v1 with a CEF-shaped v2. Rejected because the M1.1 anti-corruption boundary remains valid and CEF must stay replaceable.
Use browser events for permission or download decisions. Rejected because EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC.
Make OSR/wgpu part of M1.2 acceptance. Rejected because it would couple browser correctness to the later composition milestone.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact finite production defaults for page, queue, capture and timeout budgets are selected in the ADR/plan task and then frozen before implementation; tests use injected small limits.
Real Linux/macOS CEF packaging and headful evidence.
Production OSR/wgpu composition and final page-surface ownership.
Persistent Chromium profile migration/rollback beyond the compatibility guarantees of the pinned CEF release.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clean host installs and activates the pinned CEF package, discovers capabilities through the broker, creates a persistent context/page, renders a loopback page in a native window, observes navigation, queries AX semantics, performs exact input/click, reads a capture artifact, crashes a renderer, restores with a newer revision, hard-kills the provider, restarts with fresh RuntimeId, restores state/cookie, rejects all stale refs and exits without orphan processes.
A malicious CEF child inherits hostile arguments/environment but cannot open Worldline IPC, issue host requests, publish capabilities or reuse the provider runtime's opaque authority.
A crash occurs after CEF commit but before durable generation/completion; the caller observes Incomplete, no old generation is reused, and recovery reserves again before page readiness.
A permission callback arrives without a stored decision; it is denied synchronously and an optional event reports the outcome without influencing it.
Queue, query or capture limits are saturated under an injected small configuration; admission fails explicitly and memory/backlog remains bounded.
